title: Cheese and Potato Pasty
subtitle: A hearty shortcrust pasty of cheddar and soft potato
excerpt: Waxy potato and plenty of mature cheddar packed into a crisp shortcrust parcel. A solid vegetarian lunch that holds together well hot or cold.
sourceNotes: British pasty tradition adapted to a cheese and potato filling, common across the Midlands and Northern counties.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked or fully baked. Reheat baked pasties from frozen at 180C for 20 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze half unbaked. Bake straight from frozen with an extra 10 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pasties and chill for up to 24 hours before baking.

content.text: This is a simple pasty with a filling of cooked potato and sharp cheddar. The potato must be fully cooked before it goes in or the centre stays hard. Let the filling cool before crimping or the pastry will go greasy.
Cook the potato in salted boiling water for 8 minutes until just tender. Drain well and leave to steam dry for 5 minutes.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Remove from the heat.
Combine the potato, onion, cheddar and mustard in a bowl. Season well. Leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line the baking tray with baking paper. Divide the pastry into four equal pieces. Roll each into a circle about 20cm across.
Spoon a quarter of the filling onto one half of each pastry circle, leaving a 2cm border. Brush the border with beaten egg.
Fold the pastry over the filling. Press the edges firmly together and crimp. Place on the baking tray. Chill for 20 minutes.
Brush the tops with beaten egg. Cut a small slit in each. Bake for 35 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes before eating.

items.cause: The potato was too wet or the filling went in warm.
items.fix: Drain and steam-dry the potato properly and cool the filling fully before filling the pastry.

items.symptom: The pasty splits open during baking.
items.cause: The edges were not sealed firmly, or the filling was overfilled.
items.fix: Press the crimped edge with a fork and do not overfill. Chilling before baking helps the seal hold.

items.symptom: The pastry is pale after 35 minutes.
items.cause: The oven was not hot enough or the glaze was applied too thinly.
items.fix: Give a second coat of egg glaze and return to the oven for 5 more minutes.
